snapshot.title: TNPSC Polity: State Executive & Legislature
snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ TNPSC Polity Hook: 234: TN Seats. 1986: Council abolished. 165: Advocate General. 35: Age. Governor: Nominal.

quick_notes.title: The Governor (Art 153)
quick_notes.detail: Nominal Head of State. Appointed by President. Term : 5 years (Pleasure of President). Min Age : 35.
quick_notes.explanation: The Governor is the constitutional head of a state in India, meaning they are the formal leader but do not have real executive power, which is held by the Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers. Article 153 of the Indian Constitution states that there shall be a Governor for each state. The Governor is appointed by the President of India, not elected by the people. The Governor holds office for a term of five years, but this term is subject to the pleasure of the President, meaning the President can remove the Governor at any time without giving a reason. To be eligible for appointment as Governor, a person must be at least 35 years old. The Governor's role is largely ceremonial, like signing bills into law, but they also have certain discretionary powers in special situations, such as recommending President's Rule.

quick_notes.title: Chief Minister (Art 164)
quick_notes.detail: Real Head of State. Appointed by Governor. Head of State Council of Ministers.
quick_notes.explanation: The Chief Minister is the real head of the state government, meaning the person who actually leads the state's daily administration, even though the Governor is the ceremonial head of the state. Article 164 of the Indian Constitution says that the Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor from the party or coalition that has a majority in the State Legislative Assembly. The Chief Minister also heads the State Council of Ministers, which is the group of ministers responsible for different government departments in the state.

quick_notes.title: TN Legislative Assembly
quick_notes.detail: Unicameral (One house). Total Seats : 234 + 1 (Nominated - now removed). Quorum : 1/10th.
quick_notes.explanation: The Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly is the law-making body for the state of Tamil Nadu. It is unicameral, which means it has only one house or chamber, unlike some other states that have two houses. The total number of seats in the Assembly is 234, plus there was previously one seat for a nominated member, but that nominated seat has now been removed, so only the 234 elected members remain. For the Assembly to conduct its official business, a minimum number of members must be present; this minimum is called the quorum, and it is set at one-tenth of the total members, meaning at least 23 or 24 members must be in the house for any decision to be valid.

quick_notes.title: Legislative Council (Abolished)
quick_notes.detail: TN Legislative Council was abolished on Nov 1, 1986 (MGR government).
quick_notes.explanation: The Tamil Nadu Legislative Council was the upper house of the state legislature, meaning it was a second chamber that reviewed laws proposed by the lower house, the Legislative Assembly. TN stands for Tamil Nadu. This council was abolished, or permanently removed, on November 1, 1986, when M.G. Ramachandran, known as MGR, was the Chief Minister of the state. The abolition meant that Tamil Nadu became a state with only one legislative house, called a unicameral legislature. This change was made official through a resolution passed by the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly.

quick_notes.title: Advocate General (Art 165)
quick_notes.detail: Highest Law Officer of the State. Appointed by Governor.
quick_notes.explanation: Advocate General (Article 165) The Advocate General is the highest legal officer for a state government in India. The Governor of the state appoints this officer. Article 165 of the Indian Constitution says the Governor must appoint a person who is qualified to be a judge of a High Court, meaning they must have been a lawyer for at least ten years or a High Court judge for at least five years. The main duty of the Advocate General is to give legal advice to the state government and to perform any legal functions that the Governor assigns. This officer can also represent the state in court cases. The Advocate General holds the position at the pleasure of the Governor, meaning the Governor can remove them at any time without giving a reason.
